what: What is stopping us, in plain words. Hand-written because a machine cannot say who is waiting on whom. A blocker that clears is DELETED, not marked done.

blockers.what: One sector is still missing, and it is on our home page
blockers.why: The weekly job is fixed and redeployed — it had been dying on a file that was never in the container, before its first line. But the step that repairs our sector labels was deployed a week ago and has never once run, because that same crash killed it every Sunday. So we can still name eight sectors where we could name eleven. Getting the eleventh back means copying labels into the master database: an ordinary write, but a write.
blockers.ask: Say go and I do it. The alternative is asking a model to re-derive them, which prices at about 136 dollars and is not worth it.

blockers.what: Some of the companies we grade ourselves against won a fund that no longer exists
blockers.why: Nine so far — and nine is what one workstream happened to trip over, not a count. Those are answers nobody could ever get right, and until yesterday they sat in our denominator making one number look better than the product is. Being counted properly now. When it is done you get two figures, not one: what we grade against, and how much of it is unreachable by anyone.
blockers.ask: Nothing yet. The count comes to you with the argument, and changing what we grade against is your call, not mine.
